note: Both sets capture the same core facts — design point CP = 0.489 and CT = 0.804, the Region 3 plateaus (gen. torque 20 MN-m, generator power 15 MW, rotor speed ~7 RPM), TSR 20→3 and blade pitch 0→22° — and both contain the same internally contradictory rotor-thrust reading at 10 m/s (2.25 MN alongside 2.7 MN in A, 2.8 MN in B). Set A is the cleaner extraction: it repeats far fewer facts (two duplicate pairs versus four in B, where TSR = 20 at 3 m/s, design-point CP = 0.489, blade pitch 0° over 7–10 m/s and generator torque 20 MN-m each appear twice) and gives the Region 2 ranges for CP ≈ 0.5 and CT ≈ 0.8 instead of only single points. Set B's only real advantage is a slightly better endpoint reading of rotor thrust at 25 m/s (1.0 MN vs A's 0.9 MN).
remarks: Page is a three-panel curve figure with no data labels, so every numeric claim is a chart reading and every quote is only an axis label/legend entry; neither set's quotes can actually substantiate the plotted values. Both sets assert two different rotor-thrust values at 10 m/s (2.25 vs 2.7/2.8 MN) — the curve peaks near 2.8 MN at the rated point just right of 10 m/s, so 2.25 MN is the low/wrong one in both. Minor shared approximations not counted as wrong: rotor thrust at 25 m/s reads ~1.0 MN (A says 0.9) and power coefficient at ~17 m/s reads ~0.2 (both say 0.1). Both sets also miss the caption's attribution of the performance to the ROSCO controller, and both use the generic attribute name "value" for several claims.
